about: The coverage each assembly reaches, held in both directions. A score under its entry is a suite that weakened; a score over its entry is an entry that has stopped describing the tree it sits in, and both are refused. Checked by .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js, which the coverage workflow runs. One entry per assembly, never one number for the repository: the host project's pages and controllers are covered through API tests, and a combined figure would let engine coverage fall while the total held steady.
howToRaise: A floor is measured, never chosen. Run the coverage command below and write the percentage the check prints for that assembly. Raise a floor in the same change that raises the coverage; a floor above the measured score reds the check immediately, which is the mistake this sentence exists to prevent, and since #188 a floor left under the measured score reds it too, so the sentence is now held rather than only written. Do not round the report's rate attribute down by hand. A rate is written to at most four decimal places and the attribute carries the float form of that value, so 0.9583 is stored as 0.9582999999999999, and rounding those digits down records a hundredth less than the suite reaches. That is where two of the four entries below sat until this file was corrected. The printed percentage is the same rate multiplied by a hundred and rounded to two decimals, which moves nothing while the report keeps to four, and the check compares the rate itself with a billionth of a point of slack for the float form, so a floor taken off the printed row compares equal rather than above. A collector that starts writing a fifth decimal would break that, and the repair then is to read the rate rather than the row.
command: dotnet test --configuration Release --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults && node .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js TestResults

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.measured: line-rate 0.9404 and branch-rate 1 on the <package> tag of coverage.cobertura.xml, from the command above run on Windows against the branch giving the two collection ports a server side, with 1083 tests passing on each leg. THE LINE FLOOR WENT UP AND EVERY LINE THAT ARRIVED IS EXECUTED. LibraryManagerCollectionOwnership and LibraryManagerMembershipWriter are the server side of the two ports a refresh writes a collection through, and both are at line-rate 1 and add no unreached line: the assembly went from 744 of 800 sequence points to 884 of 940, so a hundred and forty executed lines arrive and the fifty-six that were never executed are the same fifty-six. Branch coverage is unmoved at 1, which is the direction to read carefully rather than the flat one: the two adapters DO branch, on a collection that is not there, on an item that is not a folder, on an empty identifier list and on a parent that is not set, and every one of those arms is reached by a test, so the figure stays at 1 rather than staying there for want of branches. What made them reachable at all is FakeServer, which builds a stand-in for a server interface at run time and refuses any member a test did not name, so an ILibraryManager costs a dictionary of the three members this plugin uses rather than eighty-four method bodies. Both target frameworks were measured and the two reports carry these same two rates. The machine has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg ran on the .NET 10 runtime under DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major, which means the two builds agreed rather than two runtimes. THE FIGURES THIS ENTRY CARRIED BEFORE were line-rate 0.93 and branch-rate 1, taken against the branch running a compiled query with 937 tests passing on each leg; that entry's account of which lines were unexecuted is superseded by the note below rather than restated here.

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.branchNote: NO PARTIALLY COVERED BRANCH POINT IS LEFT IN THIS ASSEMBLY, which is what the branch figure of 1 says and is the one direction of this entry that cannot rise again. A branch added tomorrow that no test reaches reds this entry immediately rather than eroding a fraction. The evaluation adapter that lowered the line figure adds no branch point at all, which is why the two figures moved in different directions in one change. THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE described a six-clause name check in RuleDocumentStore as the only partial point and read: Every partially covered branch point left in this assembly is in RuleDocumentStore, at branch-rate 0.875. That check is now a predicate the store and the API both ask, and both of its answers are reached from both callers, which is what closed it.

The stage that reads a rule's order, the table that says which fields have one, the comparison the order is built from and the two types they answer with are all reached: every refusal the stage raises is reached by a document written to trip it, including the one that needs a fixture vocabulary, and both arms of the absence rule are reached by a comparison handed its pair each way round. The assembly went from 3976 of 3978 sequence points and 1262 of 1264 branch slots to 4418 of 4420 and 1434 of 1436, so four hundred and forty-two executed lines and a hundred and seventy-two covered branch slots arrive and nothing unexecuted arrives with them. THE ONE UNREACHED ARM IS STILL THE ONLY ONE and is the same discard the branch note describes. Both target frameworks were measured and the two reports carry these same two rates. The machine has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg ran on the .NET 10 runtime under DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major, which means the two builds agreed rather than two runtimes. Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.branchNote: The only partially covered branch point in the assembly is still the discard in the value-kind description in RuleDocumentValidator, reported at condition-coverage 87.5% (7/8). The compiler requires it for exhaustiveness and no input reaches it, because a member that is absent is refused before anything describes its kind. Its line number is not recorded here any more: it moves whenever anything is added above it in that file, and it has moved twice for that reason without the arm itself changing. Read it off the report rather than from this note. The second describer beside it, added with the name member, has both arms reached and adds no partial point, and the id member's own refusals add none either: every arm of the set check, the length check and the two kind checks is reached by a test. The value types add no partial point either. Every arm of every reader is reached: each type has a test accepting its form and a test refusing the value the neighbouring type would accept, the duration walk is reached at each of its refusals including the years-and-months arm and the overflow, and both arms of the bound that cuts a quoted value are reached, by a value at the bound and by one whose cut would otherwise land inside a surrogate pair. The operator table adds no partial point either. Both arms of the acceptance walk are reached, by a pair the table accepts and by one it does not; both arms of the value-type refusal are reached, by an operator that takes a value and by one that takes none; and the two arms that throw rather than answer, an operator with no row and a refusal asked for a pair the table accepts, are each reached by a test. The composition stage adds no partial point either. Every refusal in the walk is reached by a document written to trip it, both directions of the group-count check are reached by an object carrying one member and by one carrying two, the depth arm is reached at the deepest allowed level and one past it, and the member walk is reached by a condition, by a nested group and by a member that is not an object. The field vocabulary adds no partial point either. Both arms of the row walk in the table are reached, by a field that has a row and by one that does not; both arms of the name lookup are reached, by a declared name and by a name differing from one only by case; and every arm of the stage that reads a condition's field is reached, by a condition naming a declared field, by one carrying no field member, by one whose field is not a string, by one naming a field the table does not declare and by a nested group holding each of those. The pointer resolver's arms are reached the same way: an empty pointer, a pointer with no leading slash, an absent member, an index past the end of an array, a token that is not a number, a descent into a value that is neither object nor array, and both escapes in the order the standard decodes them. The operator table's second type column adds no partial point either, and it is the one entry here where every arm is a copy of an arm already described: both directions of the field-type walk are reached, by an operator that applies to a field of the type asked about and by one that does not, and both arms of the field-type refusal are reached, by a pair the table refuses and by the accepted pair it throws for rather than answers. The stage that reads a condition's operator adds no partial point either. Every arm of it is reached by a document written to trip it: a condition with no operator member, one whose operator is a number rather than a string, one naming an operator no operator has, one naming an operator that does not apply to a field of that field's type, one naming an operator the field's own row does not declare, and one that is accepted. The two narrowed refusals beside it are reached the same way, including both arms of the guard that throws rather than building a refusal for a pair the field accepts. The stage that reads a condition's value adds no partial point either. Every arm of it is reached by a document written to trip it: a condition writing no value where the operator takes one, a condition writing no value where the operator takes a list, a value beside an operator that takes none, an operator that takes none and is written correctly, a list where one value belongs, one value where a list belongs, an empty list, a member of a list that does not parse beside members that do, and a value that does not parse where one belongs. The dispatch beside it is reached at each of its seven arms and at the throw a type with no reader takes, and the third column on the operator table is reached in both directions, by an operator written with a list and by one written with a value. The type a value is parsed against is reached on both of its answers, the field's own type and the operator's single one, and on both ways of asking for a pair that has no answer. The compile table and the stage that walks a rule's conditions onto a query add no partial point either. Both arms of the pair lookup are reached, by a pair the table compiles and by one over a field it compiles with an operator it does not; both arms of the property claim are reached, by a document narrowing two properties and by one narrowing a property another condition already wrote; both arms of every write that can decline are reached, by a value the property carries and by one it cannot, and the year check is reached at each of its two comparisons; and both arms of the guard on the write are reached, by a query and by a null one. The reporting arm in MembershipApplier adds no partial point either. Each of its three levels is asked whether it is enabled before the line is built, and both the level test and the outcome test above it are reached on both answers: a collection whose membership moved, one the run left exactly as it was, and one whose apply threw, each against a logger that reports every level enabled. The evaluation adds no partial point either, and the two arms that would have added one are the reason its own types are shaped the way they are. The shape dispatch is split off the entry point that reads an item, so a reading of a shape nothing produces can be handed to it and its last arm executed; the reading's constructor is internal exactly wide enough for that fixture. The walk over a composition group ends on the negation rather than on a throw, because a group kind with no arm cannot be written in a document at all and an arm for one could never be executed. Every other arm is reached by a pair a document can write: each of the eight comparisons over one string, the two over a list of them, the eight over a number, the three over an instant and the four over a length of time, each in both directions; the two operators about absence on both answers; a value the library does not hold on every shape that can be absent; a list the library holds as a null and one it holds as empty; an instant with no kind and one in local time; and the refusal each shape raises for an operator it has no comparison for, over five fields whose own rows do not declare that operator. The order and the cap add no partial point either. Every arm of the stage that reads them is reached by a document written to trip it: a sort that is not an array, an empty one, a term that is not an object, a term with no field and one whose field is not a string, a field the vocabulary does not declare, a field whose value is a list, a field that means nothing for anything the rule collects, a term with no direction and one whose direction is not a string, a direction no name is written under, a field named twice, a cap that is not a whole number, a cap below one, and a cap written with no order beside one written with one. The comparison the order is built from is reached on each of the four shapes it declares an order over, on the shape it declares none over, on both directions, and on both arms of the absence rule, which is reached with the pair handed to it each way round because a sort hands a comparison its pair in whichever order its own algorithm reached them in.
